literal: Holding a learned discourse before those who are not one's own peers is like nectar spilled inside a dirty drain.
translation: Holding a learned discourse before those who are not one's peers is like spilling divine nectar into a dirty drain.
modern: தம்முடைய அறிவுத் தரத்திற்குச் சமமில்லாதவர்கள் முன்னிலையில் அறிவார்ந்த சொற்பொழிவு ஆற்றுவது, சாக்கடையில் அமுதத்தைக் கொட்டுவதற்கு ஒப்பானதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of choosing the right audience for sharing high wisdom. The poet compares precious, refined knowledge to 'அமிழ்து' (divine nectar). Speaking such profound truths before 'தங்கணத்தார் அல்லார்' (those who are not one's intellectual peers) is a waste of effort. It is compared to spilling nectar into an 'அங்கணம்' (a dirty drain or sewer), where its purity and value are instantly ruined. Therefore, a wise person must only hold a discourse ('கோட்டி கொளல்') in an assembly of equals who can appreciate it.
